record.paper_title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
record.original_question: Suppose that A is a non-unital Banach lattice algebra. Let \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) be unital Banach lattice algebras, containing A as a sublattice and subalgebra, such that the smallest unital sublattice and subalgebra of \(B_k\) containing A is the whole of \(B_k\) ( \(k=1,2\) ). Is it true that for all \(x\in A\) , \(\sigma _{B_1}(x)=\sigma _{B_2}(x)\) ? The same question is of interest if \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) are restricted to be Banach lattice algebras with identities of norm 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a non-unital Banach lattice algebra; that is, $A$ is simultaneously a Banach lattice and an associative algebra whose norm is submultiplicative and in which the product of two positive elements is positive, with no multiplicative identity. Suppose $B_1$ and $B_2$ are unital Banach lattice algebras (Banach lattice algebras possessing a multiplicative identity) such that, for each $k\in\{1,2\}$, $A$ is a subalgebra and a sublattice of $B_k$ and the smallest sublattice of $B_k$ that is also a subalgebra containing $A$ and the identity of $B_k$ is all of $B_k$. For $x\in A$ and $k\in\{1,2\}$, let $\sigma_{B_k}(x)$ denote the spectrum of $x$ in $B_k$, i.e. the set of scalars $\lambda$ such that $\lambda\mathbf{1}_{B_k}-x$ is not invertible in $B_k$.

(a) Is it always the case that $\sigma_{B_1}(x)=\sigma_{B_2}(x)$ for every $x\in A$?

(b) Does the same conclusion hold under the additional restriction that the identity of each $B_k$ has norm $1$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem concerns whether two unital Banach lattice algebra envelopes of a non-unital Banach lattice algebra $A$ give the same spectrum for elements of $A$. Sources note that the standard unitization trick for Banach algebras does not transfer to Banach lattice algebras and that there is no canonical unital lattice envelope; the question is listed among open problems in the literature on Banach lattice algebras and no resolution was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Banach lattice algebras: some questions, but very few answers
status_evidence.snippet: Given a non-unital Banach algebra A embedded in a unital Banach algebra B, the linear span of A and the identity in B is a unital Banach algebra and (up to renorming) independent of the choice of B. Nothing similar works for Banach lattice algebras.
status_evidence.claim: The analogous unitization independence for Banach lattice algebras is not known to hold and is posed as an open question.
